## v5.1.0 — mentions, thread unreads, and labels on every message

![After the weekend I had, and now the printer is acting up. One search, and the PIN that had been waiting in #facilities for five months.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jtalk22/slack-mcp-server/v5.1.0/docs/images/hero-v2.gif)

Put your agent inside your Slack. Zero bots, zero admin queues, no Business+ upgrade — 20+ tools for stealth search, thread parsing and mention tracking. Every message attributed. Your session never leaves your Mac.

```sh
npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp --setup
```

### Mentions and thread replies

Every mention, every unread reply, every thread, in every conversation. The catch-up now reads the same counts Slack's own sidebar badges use, so what your agent reports is what Slack itself knows is waiting. Mentions come first. Replies in threads you were never pinged on are counted. Conversations past the first page of the listing are found and named.

In a workspace with a hundred channels, that is the difference between an agent that shows you the three channels you happened to open and one that knows every update. Catching up is now something you can hand off.

It reads `client.counts`, the undocumented endpoint behind Slack's own badges; if that call fails, the catch-up falls back to the previous view and says what is missing, so an answer is never silently incomplete.

### Author labels

Author attribution on every message, at no extra API call. Each message carries `origin` — `self`, `internal`, `external`, `bot` — and `author_trusted`. A Slack Connect message from another company, a guest, an app relaying an email or an RSS feed: your agent sees which words came from inside your organisation and which did not, before it acts on any of them.

Built for real workspaces. Slack leaves the `team` field off messages written by your own colleagues, so a naive classifier calls most of a normal channel unknown. This one reads the conversation's sharing status first: a channel Slack marks as not shared cannot contain an outside author, so a colleague without a team field is still a colleague. `unknown` is reserved for the genuinely unplaceable. On a real channel, unknowns went from more than half the messages to none.

### Read-only mode

**`--read-only` / `SLACK_MCP_READ_ONLY=1`.** The four write tools are withheld from `tools/list` and refused at dispatch if a client calls one anyway. No prompt, no label, no model behaviour is involved: the tool does not exist in that process. For a shared agent, a CI job, or a workspace where you want eyes and never hands, this is the guarantee.

### Security doctor

**`--doctor --security`.** Six checks — where the credential sits, the file's permissions, provenance mode, whether the write tools are registered, profile isolation, credential age — each with a pass, warn or fail and the one command that tightens it. No score, and it says why.

### Also new

- **Commitments, owner gaps and open questions** from `slack_catch_me_up` — who said they would do what, which asks nobody claimed, which questions are still open — each row with the text that matched and a permalink to the message.
- **`slack_session_report`** — what this process read and tried to send, as counts by origin. Never message text, never a channel name.
- **`externally_shared` on every conversation** from `slack_list_conversations`, so an agent can tell a Slack Connect channel from an internal one before it reads a word.
- **A published prompt-injection corpus** ([docs/INJECTION-CORPUS.md](https://github.com/jtalk22/slack-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/INJECTION-CORPUS.md)) — bidi overrides, zero-width splits, tool-call mimicry, bot relays, attacker-settable identity fields — so other MCP authors can test their own servers against the same attacks.
- **CodeQL and OSV-Scanner** on every change, and signed npm provenance on every release: `npm audit signatures` verifies the chain.

### Fixed

- The strict send hold could be switched off by the call it was meant to restrain, and `slack_catch_me_up` never armed it at all.
- The setup wizard described an extraction path the code does not run, and repeated one fixed instruction whatever the failure. It now follows the reason code and prints the client configuration instead of linking to a page about it.
- Commands an `npx` user cannot run were removed from the docs and the bug-report template.
- Identity-keyed caches are cleared on a token refresh; a refresh can land on a different workspace.
- `slack_catch_me_up` and `slack_conversations_history` classified the same message differently; both now resolve the conversation's sharing state.

### Security

**Hardened before release.** An independent review of this release's code ran before it shipped, with probes rather than reading alone. It found five ways the new guarantees could be narrower than their descriptions, and all five are closed in this build, each with a regression test:

- The strict hold now counts outside-authored replies inside threads the catch-up expands, not just top-level messages.
- A credential refresh clears the workspace identity caches, so a session that lands on a different workspace can never label its authors by the old one.
- DM discovery, which opens conversations, is refused in read-only mode along with the four write tools.
- A malformed `client.counts` response degrades to the listing view instead of failing the whole read.
- A message carrying a foreign team id is never placed as a colleague, whatever the sharing state says, when the identity lookup has failed.

Each is tracked as a closed issue with the test that pins it. The review's full write-up and the before/after probes are linked from the issues.

A provenance label is advice to the calling model: unsigned, strippable downstream. The `strict` hold is released by a flag the caller sets, so it records a send without proving a human approved it. Display names and channel topics still reach the model unlabelled. `--read-only` is the only guarantee that does not depend on the model. All of it is in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/jtalk22/slack-mcp-server/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

### Compatibility

Default behaviour adds keys and removes none. `SLACK_MCP_PROVENANCE=off` restores the previous output shape. The `provenance` argument on a read may tighten labelling and no longer loosen it. Node 20 and up.

### Install

```sh
npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp --setup
claude mcp add slack -- npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp
```

```sh
npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp --doctor --security   # check your own setup
npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp --read-only           # read Slack, never write to it
```

Full changelog: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/jtalk22/slack-mcp-server/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#510---2026-10-07)
